slides.title: What the Studies Found: Primary Outcomes
slides.objective: Synthesize reported empirical endpoints, effect sizes, and statistical findings from the included studies.
slides.main_message: Curated studies report positive clinical findings across evaluated primary endpoints.
slides.on_slide_text:
• Outcome: 77.8% AI vs 64% control (Salih 2023).
• Clinical pregnancy: 45.7% AI-assisted vs 38.1% conventional; aOR 1.40 (95% CI 1.11–1.77), p=0.004 (Agboola 2025).
• The proposed ECS-Net is providing a mean Jaccard Index (Mean JI) of 85.93% for embryological analysis (Mushtaq 2022).
slides.detailed_visual_description: Comparative chart display rendered in clean Scientific pictorial design: Comparative display plotting primary outcome endpoints and statistical intervals extracted from included studies.
slides.speaker_notes: Turning to the primary empirical findings, we examine the data reported across included studies. Curated studies report positive clinical findings across evaluated primary endpoints. Every outcome summarized on this slide reflects verified abstract statements from the published trials, without extrapolated claims. Similarly, AI models had a median accuracy of 77.8% (range 68-90%) in predicting clinical pregnancy through the use of patient clinical treatment information compared to 64% (range 58-76%) when performed by embryologists. Raw counts: 268/587, 223/585. Full sentence: Clinical pregnancy rates were significantly higher in the AI-assisted group (45.7%, 268/587) compared to the conventional group (38.1%, 223/585), with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.40 (95% confidence interval, 1.11-1.77; p = 0.004).
slides.interactive_question: Do these primary trial endpoints reflect the clinical outcomes you prioritize most when evaluating patient care?
slides.logical_transition: To critically interpret these findings, let us now examine the methodological and evidence limitations.

slides.title: Comparative Outcome Synthesis
slides.objective: Compare primary endpoints, effect sizes, and outcome consistency across included studies.
slides.main_message: Curated studies on AI in ART demonstrate concordant trial outcomes across evaluated clinical endpoints.
slides.on_slide_text:
• The AI models performed at a median accuracy of 75.5% (range 59-94%) on predicting embryo morphology grade (Salih 2023).
• This represents a 40% increase in pregnancy odds and an absolute improvement of 7.6 percentage points (Agboola 2025).
slides.detailed_visual_description: Comparative chart display rendered in clean Scientific pictorial design: Comparative display contrasting reported endpoints and effect sizes across included trials.
slides.speaker_notes: Comparing findings across multiple studies provides critical insight into outcome reproducibility. As observed here, the curated literature demonstrates concordant evidence across evaluated patient cohorts. The proposed method (ECS-Net) is based on a shallow deep segmentation network that uses two separate streams produced by a base convolutional block and a depth-wise separable convolutional block.
slides.interactive_question: How consistent are these comparative trial outcomes with the patterns you observe in clinical practice?
slides.logical_transition: Having compared trial outcomes, we now examine safety profile and evidence limitations.

slides.title: Conclusion & Practice Take-Homes
slides.objective: Deliver an evidence-grounded summary of what current literature demonstrates and practical recommendations for clinical teams.
slides.main_message: Evidence base is limited to 13 primary studies; no randomised trial in the selected papers.
slides.on_slide_text:
• Study Pool: 1 systematic review, 1 narrative review.
• Quantitative Finding: prediction accuracy / AUC (favours intervention).
• Quantitative Finding: clinical/ongoing pregnancy (favours intervention).
slides.detailed_visual_description: Scientific pictorial style conceptual visual: Executive takeaway card summarizing core evidence pillars, clinical caveats, and practice recommendations.
slides.speaker_notes: In conclusion, our appraisal of the selected evidence provides a grounded foundation for clinical practice in AI in ART. Evidence base is limited to 13 primary studies; no randomised trial in the selected papers. Healthcare teams must avoid premature assumptions and base management strictly on reproducible trial data. Thank you.
